findings.evidence: The corrected architecture now defines the required deterministic mechanism: server-owned exact persisted Section spans, immutable text/support signatures, provider selection/order handles only, fixed server citations, immediate revalidation, and whole-answer rejection for foreign, unrelated, contradictory-decoy, swapped, or changed candidates. However, plan.md:399 still states that the closed provider JSON permits claim text and opaque citation handles and applies a narrative locator validator. That directly contradicts plan.md:176 and 218-223, data-model.md:118-119, and chat-agent-contract.md:124-140, where provider-authored claim text and citation selection are forbidden. Because this stale statement reintroduces the exact unsafe design rejected in iteration 1, the complete raw plan set does not provide one unambiguous implementation contract.
findings.exact_correction_outcome: Replace plan.md:399 so the mitigation permits only schema/request/mode/fingerprint echoes and unique ordered Candidate Claim handles, with no provider-authored claim text, citation handle, locator, narrative, or diagnostic. State that Business locator safety is applied to server-extracted Candidate Claim text before dispatch and revalidated before render. Perform a complete-plan consistency sweep so every provider-output statement matches the selection-only schema. Preserve the exact-span/support-signature and whole-answer adversarial tests already added.

findings.evidence: The correction now assigns sole harness ownership; keeps the clean database alive; provisions users, roles, scope, providers, assignments, and knowledge through product services; shares a Data Protection ring/application discriminator; specifies an isolated Worker/Chat fixture; uses real Identity and Playwright over an interactive Blazor circuit; supplies a curl health command available in the runtime image; asserts positive citations plus negative revocation; and requires finally cleanup with database absence. Two executable defects remain. First, plan.md:368-372 says Worker/Chat servers bind only to container loopback while the host reaches those ports through Docker publishing. A socket listening only on the provider container's 127.0.0.1 is not reachable through ordinary published-port forwarding to the container interface, so the host-side profiling/Scan path cannot call the stored loopback providers as described. Second, quickstart.md:67-81 builds only Vulgata.Web in Release and then claims that build restores the test-only Playwright package before invoking tests/Vulgata.Tests/bin/Release/net10.0/playwright.ps1. The Web build does not build the test project, while the earlier focused test commands use the default configuration; therefore the referenced Release script is not produced on a clean run. The final browser gate remains non-runnable as written.
findings.exact_correction_outcome: Specify one concrete reachable provider/app topology and exact arguments. For example, have the provider listen on all interfaces inside its nonce-owned namespace, publish Worker/Chat ports only on host 127.0.0.1 for host-side Scan calls, launch the final app in that provider namespace so stored 127.0.0.1 endpoints resolve, and publish the shared namespace's app port for Playwright; alternatively move every caller into the same namespace. Do not claim a container-loopback-only listener is reachable through a published port. Add an explicit restore/build of tests/Vulgata.Tests in Release before invoking its generated Playwright installer, or consistently use the configuration whose script was actually generated. Keep the newly specified product-service provisioning, shared Data Protection, real Identity/circuit assertions, curl health, positive/negative checks, and complete cleanup.

constitution_result.evidence: Layer ownership, specific repository boundaries, immutable current Document use, no-migration intent, Chinese UI, embedded prompts, encrypted provider secrets, source isolation, double authorization, and exact Cross-Repository truth remain compatible with the Constitution. Principle IV cannot pass while the mandatory final provider/browser path is not executable from the documented commands. Principle V cannot pass while one authoritative plan sentence still allows provider-authored claim text and citation handles. No ADR or context-specific ADR exists at the pinned boundary; root CONTEXT-MAP.md is absent, matching the plan's recorded existing condition rather than introducing a conflict.
